name: ExecV2
description: Use this instead of the Bash tool. Execute commands as a structured tree, not a shell string. A `pipeline` is either a single command `{ id, program, args }` or an operation `{ op, left, right }` joining two pipelines. `op` is one of: `;` run both in sequence, `&&` run right only if left exits 0, `||` run right only if left is non-zero, `&` run both concurrently, `|` pipe left's stdout into right's stdin. Each command's `id` is echoed on its result entry so you can match results to commands.

intent.description: Human-readable summary of what these commands do, so the user can understand the intent at a glance.

stripAnsi.description: Strip ANSI escape codes from output (default: true). Set false to preserve raw color/formatting codes.

id.description: Caller-assigned identifier copied verbatim to this leaf's result entry.

program.description: The program, binary, or script path to execute. Supports ~ and $VAR expansion. Must be on $PATH or an absolute path.

args.description: Arguments to the program. Each argument is a separate string — no shell quoting or escaping needed.

path.description: File path to redirect output to. Supports ~ and $VAR expansion.

append.description: Append to file instead of overwriting

cwd.description: Working directory for this command. Supports ~ and $VAR expansion.

env.description: Environment variables to set for this command.

merge_stderr.description: Merge stderr into stdout (equivalent to 2>&1). Combined output appears in stdout; stderr will be empty.

op.description: Operator: ';' sequence, '&&' and, '||' or, '&' concurrent, '|' pipe
